CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation for breast reduction surgery.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female presenting as a new consult for breast reduction. She has been considering this procedure for approximately 6-7 years. She reports symptomatic macromastia with multiple complaints including back pain, neck pain, and upper back pain since high school. She experiences bra strap indentations on her shoulders and wears a 34E sports bra as it is more comfortable than regular bras. She occasionally experiences numbness and tingling in her hands. She reports that her breasts are always sweaty but denies rashes underneath. She has activity limitations with working out, jumping, and running due to breast size and associated pain. She has been seeing a chiropractor for a few years for pain management. She has not had previous consultations for breast reduction. The patient has attempted nonsurgical treatments with minimal relief. She is eager to proceed with surgery once her insurance changes over in July.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for back pain, neck pain, upper back pain, occasional numbness and tingling in hands, and sweating under breasts. Denies rashes underneath breasts, nipple pain, or nipple discharge. Denies other systemic complaints.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
History of breast cancer in family (mother diagnosed at age 40). Patient is 25 years old and does not yet meet screening recommendations.

MEDICATIONS
Propranolol (migraine medication).

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother with breast cancer diagnosed at age 40.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is currently a psychology student. She drinks wine occasionally. Denies tobacco and drug use. She has lost 10 pounds over the past few months and desires to lose an additional 20 pounds. She is married. She does not have children but may plan to have children in the future.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Inspection reveals asymmetrical breasts with severe bilateral ptosis. One breast is noted to be slightly lower than the other. No nipple retraction or discharge noted bilaterally. No breast tenderness, masses, or axillary lymphadenopathy palpable on examination. Measurements obtained as needed for surgical planning.

RESULTS
Body surface area of 2.65. Schnur scale minimum required resection is 1,792 grams. Current bra size approximately G cup; patient desires B cup postoperatively. Examination findings consistent with severe macromastia with significant ptosis bilaterally.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female with symptomatic macromastia presenting for evaluation of breast reduction. She is an ideal candidate for bilateral reduction mammoplasty. Plan for bilateral breast reduction with nipple repositioning to relieve back and neck pain while improving aesthetic appearance. Planned procedure involves anchor-type incision around nipple with vertical and inframammary components to remove excess fat and breast tissue. Expected result is small C cup size based on blood supply constraints. Surgery anticipated to take approximately 3 hours with bilateral drains to be removed at 1 week postoperatively. Plan for one-night hospital stay for pain and nausea management. Patient counseled regarding potential inability to breastfeed (approximately 30% of patients), possible nipple sensation changes, normal postoperative bruising, activity restrictions for 6 weeks including no heavy lifting and no driving for 2-3 weeks. Advised that breasts may change with weight gain, pregnancy, and hormonal changes. Patient is ready to proceed once insurance switches in July. Plan to obtain photographs today and submit for insurance preauthorization once new insurance information is obtained. Patient will notify office with new insurance details. Follow-up appointment scheduled for right before surgery to review final instructions and answer any remaining questions.
